back_translation: Woe to those who enact unrighteous statutes and who write oppressive verdicts,
to bar the needy from fair treatment and to rob the afflicted of My people of their rightful claim, so that widows become what they plunder and the fatherless become their prey.
What will you do on the day of punishment, when devastation comes from a distant land? To whom will you flee for help? And where will you leave your riches?
There is no way left except to kneel down among the captives or fall among the slain. Even so, His wrath has not turned back, and His hand is still stretched out.
Woe to Assyria, the rod of My anger — the club in their hands is My fury!
I send him against a godless nation; I commission him against the people of My fury, to seize spoil, to snatch plunder, and to trample them down like mud in the streets.
But he does not intend it so, and his heart does not think so; for in his heart he thinks only of destroying and of cutting off many nations.
For he says: "Are not my commanders all kings?
Is not Calno like Carchemish? Is not Hamath like Arpad? And is not Samaria like Damascus?
My hand has seized the kingdoms of the idols, whose carved images surpassed those of Jerusalem and Samaria.
As I have done to Samaria and her idols, shall I not do the same to Jerusalem and her idols?"

When the Sovereign Master has finished all His royal work against Mount Zion and Jerusalem, He will punish the fruit of the arrogant heart of the king of Assyria and the haughtiness of his proud eyes.

For he says: "I have done this by the strength of my own hand and by my wisdom, for I am shrewd. I have removed the boundaries of nations, plundered the treasures in their storehouses, and brought down those who sit on thrones like a mighty bull.

My hand reached the wealth of the nations as one reaches into a bird's nest; and like someone gathering abandoned eggs, I gathered the whole earth. Not one fluttered a wing, or opened its mouth, or gave a single chirp."
Does an axe boast over the one who chops with it? Does a saw exalt itself over the one who pulls it? As if a rod could wave the one who lifts it — as if a club could lift him who is not wood!
Therefore the Sovereign Master, the LORD of Hosts, will send a wasting disease among his sturdy warriors, and beneath his overwhelming pomp a fire will be kindled like a consuming blaze.
And the Light of Israel will become a fire, and his Holy One a flame; it will burn and devour his thornbushes and his briers in a single day.
He will consume the glory of his forest and his fruitful orchard completely, both soul and body; and it will be like a sick man wasting away until his strength is gone.
The trees left in his forest will be so few that a child could write down their list.
In that day the remnant of Israel and the survivors of the house of Jacob will no longer lean on the one who struck them, but will lean on the LORD, the Holy One of Israel, in faithful sincerity.
A remnant will return — the remnant of Jacob — to the Mighty God.
O Israel, though your people be like the grains of sand of the sea, only a remnant will return. Annihilation has been decreed, flooding in with righteousness.
For the Lord GOD of Hosts will carry out the destruction that has been decreed, in the midst of the whole earth.
Therefore this is what the Lord GOD of Hosts says: "O My people who dwell in Zion, do not fear Assyria, who strikes you with a rod and raises his club against you as Egypt once did.
For in only a very little while My fury against you will come to an end, and My anger will turn to their destruction."
The LORD of Hosts will lash a whip against them, as when He struck Midian at the rock of Oreb; and His royal staff will be over the sea, and He will raise it as He did in Egypt.
In that day his burden will be lifted from your shoulder and his yoke from your neck; the yoke will be broken to pieces because of fatness.
He has reached Aiath; he has passed through Migron; he stores his baggage at Michmash.
They have crossed over the pass: "We will lodge overnight at Geba." Ramah trembles; Gibeah of Saul has fled.
Cry out with your voice, O Daughter of Gallim! Listen, O Laishah! O pitiable Anathoth!
Madmenah has fled for refuge; the people of Gebim run to hide.
This very day he will halt his army at Nob; he shakes his fist at the mountain of Daughter Zion, the hill of Jerusalem.
Behold, the Sovereign Master, the LORD of Hosts, will lop off the branches with terrifying power. The towering trees will be felled, and the lofty ones will be brought down low.
He will cut down the thick forest with an iron axe, and Lebanon will fall before the face of the Majestic One.
